title: Exact colimit-preserving evaluation at an affine weakly contractible object
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on this site, and let $W\to X$ be an affine site object which is weakly contractible: every epimorphism $F\to G$ of sheaves of sets induces a surjection $F(W)\to G(W)$. Then evaluation $\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R(W))$, $M\mapsto M(W)$, on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is exact and preserves all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. In particular, for every small filtered diagram $(M_i)$, its canonical comparison $\varinjlim_i M_i(W)\to(\varinjlim_i M_i)(W)$ is an isomorphism, natural in diagrams.

proof.text: Apply weaklyContractible_evaluation_preservesHomology to the given weak contractibility hypothesis. Evaluation is additive by its sectionwise definition, so Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesHomology and Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesHomology give finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation.

Every covering sieve on an affine pro-etale object contains a finite covering family. Extract a covering presieve using precoverage.mem_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderComposition, map its zero-hypercover to schemes, and use QuasiCompactCover.exists_hom for a finite affine refinement. Lift the refinement back to the pro-etale over-category; each composite still lies in the original sieve.

proof.text: For any small diagram of module sheaves, its presheaf-colimit comparison to the sheaf colimit is locally surjective. Apply PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction to the presheaf colimit. The left adjoint preserves this colimit, and its counit identifies the sheafified diagram with the original diagram. Uniqueness of colimits identifies the comparison with the sheafification unit followed by an isomorphism; the triangle identity verifies the identification on every inclusion. The unit is locally surjective by Mathlib’s WEqualsLocallyBijective instance.

source.place: Tags 03DB and 00WK, colimits as sheafifications and local representatives.

proof.text: Express a coproduct as the filtered colimit of its finite subcoproducts using isColimitFiniteSubproductsCocone. Local surjectivity supplies presheaf representatives on a covering, and presheaf evaluation followed by the module forgetful functor preserves this filtered colimit. Thus each local representative comes from a finite subcoproduct. Take a finite covering refinement and the union of those finite supports. The coproduct projection onto this union fixes each local representative. Naturality and separatedness show that it fixes the original section globally. Hence every section over W factors through a finite subcoproduct.

source.place: Tag 0935 (2), finite-support descent; projection replaces coordinate-by-coordinate gluing.

proof.text: Additivity makes evaluation preserve finite coproducts, so every finite sigmaComparison is invertible. The finite-support result proves surjectivity of the arbitrary sigmaComparison. For injectivity, express an element in the source coproduct as an element of a finite subcoproduct using the filtered-colimit presentation in ModuleCat. The inclusion of the corresponding finite sheaf coproduct has a projection retraction. Applying this retraction to a vanishing comparison shows that the finite comparison of the element is zero, hence the element itself is zero. ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective and PreservesCoproduct.of_iso_comparison now give arbitrary coproduct preservation. Empty supports and empty coproducts are included.

source.place: Tag 0935 (2), preservation of arbitrary direct sums.

proof.text: Finite-colimit preservation supplies preservation of coequalizers. Apply Mathlib preservesColimits_of_preservesCoequalizers_and_coproducts, whose universal-property construction presents an arbitrary small colimit as a coequalizer of two coproducts. This gives PreservesColimitsOfSize in exactly the section universe, including the empty diagram. The filtered comparison is therefore an isomorphism. Its naturality is Mathlib colimit.map_post applied to the natural transformation and evaluation functor.
